plain.li: [first] One year ago the colony was a few packs dropped in the {PLACE} and a fire that wouldn't catch. {A_nameDef} was there that first night, and still talks about the cold.
[first] {A_nameDef} has been taking the newcomers round the first shelter this morning, showing them where everyone slept. It's a year today since the colony came to the {PLACE}.
[years] Before breakfast {A_nameDef} walked the line of the old boundary, the one the colony outgrew long ago. It is {YEARS} years today since the founding.
[years] {YEARS} years in the {PLACE} today. {A_nameDef} can still point to the spot where the first fire was lit, though there's a wall over it now.
[tradition] The founding is a tradition here now, and everyone knows how {A_nameDef} will tell the story of the first night, down to the pauses.
[winter] Snow on founding day. {A_nameDef} says the first winter was far worse, and the ones who were there agree.
[lowtech,years] There are {YEARS} notches in the post by the gate now. {A_nameDef} cut the newest this morning, one for each year since the founding.

warm.li: {A_nameDef} has spent the morning going from room to room, thanking people for staying on through the bad years.

gloomy.li: It's founding day. {A_nameDef} says it's a wonder the colony is still here at all, and seems to mean it.

plain.li: [first] A year ago today the colony brought in its first real harvest. {A_nameDef} planted most of it, and has mentioned this at every meal so far today.
[years] It's {YEARS} years since the first good crop came in, and {A_nameDef} wants the day marked the way it was then, with everyone at one table.
A sheaf of grain hangs over the door this morning. {A_nameDef} put it there, and says that's how harvest day starts now.
Whatever the fields look like this year, {A_nameDef} says harvest day is for the first crop, the one that kept the colony fed.
[tradition] {A_nameDef} has been baking since before dawn, as on every harvest day since it became the custom.
[winter] Harvest day falls in the cold, with the fields bare. {A_nameDef} hauled a sack of grain up from the stores so there'd be something to put on the table.

blunt.li: Harvest day. {A_nameDef} has asked that the growers be served first tonight, and won't hear otherwise.

cheerful.li: Harvest day! {A_nameDef} has been going round with a basket of the season's best, making people guess what each one weighs.

plain.li: [first] The first snow of the winter, a year after the colony saw its very first. {A_nameDef} was out before anyone else, catching flakes on {A_possessive} sleeve.
[years] The first snow came down overnight. {A_nameDef} is already out stamping a path to the woodpile; the colony has made a day of this for {YEARS} years now.
The first snow is falling, and {A_nameDef} has been at the window since it started.
Snow is settling on the roofs, the first of the winter, and every sound outside has gone soft.
[tradition] Snow, the first of the winter. By custom here that means an afternoon of games while it settles.
[storm] The first snow of the winter came in sideways on a hard wind. {A_nameDef} says it counts all the same.

cheerful.li: First snow! {A_nameDef} has packed the first snowball of the winter and is looking for someone to throw it at.

gloomy.li: The first snow. {A_nameDef} watched it come down for a long time, then went to count the firewood.

plain.li: [clean,first] A year ago today the colony saw off {ENEMY}, and {COUNT} of them fell without the loss of one of ours. {A_nameDef} still talks about where the line held.
[clean,years] {A_nameDef} wants a feast tonight, like the one the night the colony beat back {ENEMY}, {YEARS} years ago.
[clean] {A_nameDef} walked the old defenses this morning, the ones that held against {ENEMY} on this day.
[clean,tradition] Every year at supper the fight with {ENEMY} gets told again, and every year the enemy is a little more numerous.
[nemesis,first] A year ago today {ENEMY} was finally brought down. {A_nameDef} says the colony slept better that night than it had in months.
[nemesis,years] Some of the newer people know {ENEMY} only from the stories. {A_nameDef}, who was there {YEARS} years ago, is glad to tell them again.
[fallen,first] A year ago today the colony fought {ENEMY} and lost {DEAD}. {A_nameDef} has said very little this morning.
[fallen,years] {YEARS} years since the battle with {ENEMY}, when {DEAD} fell. The ones who were there don't talk about it much, but they were all up early today.
[fallen] On this day {ENEMY} attacked, and {DEAD} did not come back from the fight. {A_nameDef} went out to the graves before breakfast.
[fallen,tradition] The colony keeps this day every year for {DEAD}, who fell fighting {ENEMY}.

blunt.li: [clean] The day {ENEMY} came and lost. {A_nameDef} says that's worth a drink.

gloomy.li: [fallen] The day of the battle with {ENEMY} has come round again. {A_nameDef} has kept to {A_possessive} room all morning.

plain.li: [first] A year ago today, {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} was up before dawn and spent the morning at the grave.
[years] {A_nameDef} will set out a cup for {DEAD} at supper tonight, as on this day every year for {YEARS} years.
[!winter] There are wildflowers on {DEAD}'s grave this morning. {A_nameDef} picked them.
[winter] Snow lay over {DEAD}'s grave until {A_nameDef} went out and cleared it this morning.
It's the day {DEAD} died. At breakfast someone told {DEAD}'s worst joke, badly, the way {DEAD} used to.
[tradition] This evening {A_nameDef} will say a few words for {DEAD}, as the colony does every year on this day.
[rain] It's the day {DEAD} died, and it's raining. {A_nameDef} went out to the grave anyway.

warm.li: {A_nameDef} has been telling the newer people about {DEAD} all morning, starting with the day they met.

blunt.li: The day {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} has asked not to be given any work today.

plain.li: [first] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were married a year ago today, and {B_nameDef} has been up since dawn on some errand {A_nameDef} isn't allowed to ask about.
[first] One year married today. {B_nameDef} remembered; {A_nameDef} needed a hint, though not much of one.
[years] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have been married {YEARS} years today. Someone found the cup they drank from at the wedding and set it on the table.
It's {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}'s wedding day. The colony would like to mark it, whatever the two of them say.
[tradition] Every year the colony marks {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}'s wedding day, and every year {A_nameDef} says there's no need.
[spring] The first flowers are out for {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}'s wedding day, and somebody has already braided a few into {B_nameDef}'s hair.
[first,named] This is the first time the colony has had {NAME} to keep, and there are as many ideas for it as there are people.
[years] The colony has kept {NAME} for {YEARS} years now, and the cooks have opinions about the menu.
It's {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has been asking since breakfast whether there'll be a feast.
Someone has already pushed the tables together for {NAME}.
[tradition] Today is {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has been setting food aside for it all week, as the custom goes.
[winter] This year {NAME} falls in the deep cold, which makes a hot meal in company sound all the better.

cheerful.li: It's {NAME}! {A_nameDef} has hung a string of dyed rags over the door and calls it bunting.

plain.li: [first,named] Today is the first {NAME}, the day the council set aside to remember the colony's dead. People aren't sure yet how it should be kept.
Today is {NAME}, set aside to remember the ones the colony has lost.
[years] {A_nameDef} has already been out to the graves for {NAME}, and left something small at each.
It's {NAME}. Work goes on, but slower, and people talk about the ones who aren't here.
[tradition] It is {NAME}, kept every year now. The older hands know which names to say without being asked.
[first,named] The first {NAME} has come, and the idea of a whole day off has gone down very well.
It's {NAME}, and the council has been asked whether the tools can stay on their hooks today.
[years] For {YEARS} years the colony has downed tools on {NAME}, and the work has always been there the next morning.
Today is {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has already found a warm spot and announced plans to stay in it.
[tradition] It's {NAME}, the colony's day of rest by long custom. The tools were hung up last night.
[trait:Industrious] It's {NAME}. {A_nameDef} is the only one who has asked what needs doing today.
[first,named] The first {NAME} is here, and {A_nameDef} has already marked out a race course and started taking bets.
It's {NAME}. Someone has set up a target behind the storehouse, and there's talk of a tug-of-war after lunch.
{A_nameDef} has been running laps of the yard every evening this week, ready for the footrace on {NAME}.
[years] The same games on {NAME} for {YEARS} years now, and the same people still cheating at them.
[tradition] It's {NAME}, and last year's winners haven't let anyone forget who they are.
[winter] Snow on {NAME} this year, so the races will be short and the snowball fight long.
[summer] It's hot for {NAME}, and the races will be run early, before the worst of the heat.
It's {A_nameDef}'s birthday today.
Somebody has saved {A_nameDef} the best seat at supper for {A_possessive} birthday.
[old] {A_nameDef} has another birthday today, and has asked that nobody count the years out loud.
[child] It's {A_nameDef}'s birthday, and {A_nameDef} has been up since dawn waiting for someone to say so.
[teen] {A_nameDef}'s birthday. {A_nameDef} says it's no big deal, and has mentioned it four times.
[lowtech] Someone has carved {A_nameDef} a wooden bird for {A_possessive} birthday.
[winter] {A_nameDef}'s birthday falls in the deep cold, and the cooks found a few sweet things to mark it anyway.

warm.li: It's {A_nameDef}'s birthday, and there are plenty of people here who owe {A_objective} a favor or two.

blunt.li: {A_nameDef}'s birthday. {A_nameDef} would like everyone to stop mentioning it.

plain.li: [first] A year ago today, {A_nameDef} came to the colony, in its first year.
[years] It's {YEARS} years since {A_nameDef} arrived, back when the colony was new.
On this day {A_nameDef} walked into a colony that was barely more than a camp.
